description: Sync issues and pull requests, each with its whole discussion, from the GitHub repositories you choose.
opening: The GitHub connector syncs issues and pull requests from selected repositories. Code, commits and diffs are not synced. Each issue and each pull request is one document that carries its body and its whole discussion: conversation comments and, for a pull request, review comments and review summaries.
Issues and pull requests link to the issues they reference or close, to their parent issue, and to the Linear issues, Slack messages and Notion pages they link to.
A private repository's items are limited to its collaborators and teams only when Enforce ACL is on and HydraDB can read its collaborators. Deleted issues and pull requests stay in HydraDB.

permissions.who_can_read: Access follows the repository, not the single issue. A public or internal repository can be read by everyone who can query the collection unless you set an access rule. A private repository can be read by its collaborators and by the organization teams that have access to it.
permissions.identity: The email address on a collaborator's public GitHub profile. Teams are added as groups.
permissions.when_unreadable: If a collaborator hides their profile email, the collaborator list is incomplete, there are too many people to express, or GitHub refuses a request, the connector reports a permission warning.
notes: One collaborator with a hidden public email stops HydraDB from capturing a private repository's audience. Set an access rule on such a repository.
Internal repositories are open to everyone who can query the collection. Check that this matches who should see them.

connect.auth: GitHub uses a personal access token. The setup steps below use a classic token, which needs `repo`, or `public_repo` for public repositories only. A fine-grained token works if GitHub grants it read access to the repositories you want and to their issues.

credentials.name: access_token
credentials.text: A GitHub personal access token with read access to repositories and issues.

permissions.name: public_repo
permissions.text: public repositories only. Use this or `repo`.

permissions.name: repo
permissions.text: private and public repositories. Reading a private repository's collaborators for permissions also needs it.

permissions.name: read:org
permissions.text: reads which organization teams can access a repository, for permissions. If GitHub refuses it, the connector reports a permission warning.

connect.permissions_note: A successful token check does not guarantee access to every repository. Confirm that the repositories you need are listed when you select them.

steps.title: Create a token
steps.text: In GitHub, create a personal access token with `repo`, or `public_repo` for public repositories only. Add `read:org` if you want organization team access captured.

steps.title: Select repositories
steps.text: HydraDB lists every repository the token's user owns, collaborates on, or can see as an organization member. Select the repositories to sync.

connect.account: One connector reads the repositories one token's user can see.

sync.first_sync: Reaches back 30 days by default, set by `lookback_days`. The window is measured from the repository's most recent activity, not from today, so a quiet repository still brings in its last stretch of work.
sync.changes: Each sync asks GitHub for items updated since the last sync. A changed item is sent again with its whole discussion.
sync.edits: Editing an issue or pull request, or adding a comment, moves its updated time, so the whole item is sent again.
sync.deletes: Deleted issues and pull requests are not removed. An item that disappears from GitHub can stay searchable in HydraDB.
notes: GitHub rate limits apply per token. A large first sync can use its hourly quota.

documents.name: Issues and pull requests
documents.one_document: One issue or one pull request, with its whole discussion inside it. A search result is the issue or pull request, not an individual comment.
documents.title: The issue or pull request title.
documents.text: The issue or pull request body and its discussion are searchable together. Comments and reviews include their author and time. Review comments also include the file, line and reply context. Empty comments are skipped. Labels are written as a `Labels` line, the creation time as a `Created` line, and a sub-issue's parent as a `Parent` line. The title is searchable too.
documents.date: When the issue or pull request was last updated.
documents.link_back: The issue or pull request page on GitHub.
documents.files: Images and files in bodies and comments are not downloaded.

attributes.name: title
attributes.text: HydraDB also scans the title for Linear issue keys and links, and links the item to those issues.

attributes.name: body
attributes.text: The main text. References in it become links: `#123`, `owner/repo#123`, closing keywords, and Linear, Slack and Notion links.

attributes.name: Comments
attributes.text: Each comment, review comment and review summary is searchable with the item. Its author is recorded as a commenter, and references inside it become links of the item.

attributes.name: labels
attributes.text: Written as the `Labels` line, so a query can match a label.

attributes.name: created_at
attributes.text: Written as the `Created` line.

attributes.name: Item id
attributes.text: The id `owner/repo#number`. It keeps later syncs on the same document, and it is what items in other tools, such as Linear issues, link to.

attributes.name: updated_at
attributes.text: When the item was last updated. It moves with every edit or new comment. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.github_repo
attributes.text: The repository as `owner/name`. Limits a query to one repository. Not searchable.

attributes.name: additional_metadata.github_issue_number
attributes.text: The issue or pull request number within a repository. Combine it with `additional_metadata.github_repo` to select one item. Not searchable.

attributes.name: connector_id
attributes.text: Limits a query to this connector's items. Not searchable.

attributes.name: provider
attributes.text: Always `github`. Not searchable.

attributes.name: parent_id
attributes.text: A sub-issue's parent issue, as `owner/repo#number`. Links the sub-issue to its parent, and is written as the `Parent` line.

attributes.name: is_pr
attributes.text: Marks a pull request, so closing keywords in its body link it to the issues it closes. Not searchable.

attributes.name: mentions
attributes.text: Each `@username` in the body, recorded as a person the item mentions. The field itself is not searchable, but the body it comes from is.

attributes.name: Repository
attributes.text: The selected repository. Its audience decides who can read every issue and pull request in it. Not searchable.

attributes.name: author
attributes.text: The login of the person who opened the item. It is not added to the graph as a person.

attributes.name: assignees
attributes.text: Assignee logins. Not added to the graph.

attributes.name: state
attributes.text: `open` or `closed`.

attributes.name: closed_at
attributes.text: When the item was closed.

attributes.name: milestone, milestone_due
attributes.text: The milestone title and its due date.

example_searches: Which issues in `acme/api` are labelled bug and mention the login timeout?
Which Linear issue does this pull request close?

connections: A sub-issue to its parent issue.
An issue or pull request to each issue or pull request it references in its body or discussion.
A pull request to each issue its body closes with a closing keyword.
An issue or pull request to a Linear issue it links to, or names after a closing word.
An issue or pull request to a Slack message or Notion page it links to.
In the other direction, Linear issues link to the GitHub pull requests attached to them.
References inside code blocks, inline code and HTML comments are ignored.
people: The author of each comment, as a commenter.
The opener and assignees are not attached to the item as people in the graph.
graph.from_text: The body and discussion text of each issue and pull request.

not_synced: Releases, wikis, projects and GitHub Discussions.
Images and files attached in bodies and comments.
Repositories the token's user cannot see.
